history.period: Modern — consecrated 24 June 1999; offered to the world 23 November 1999
history.summary: NON-CONVENTIONAL SHRINE — keep-or-drop decision needed: the Dhyanalinga is NOT a conventional Hindu temple. Per Isha/travel sources it 'does not ascribe to any particular faith or belief system nor does it require any ritual, prayer, or worship' — it is a yogic meditation space. CSV TOWN CORRECTION: 'Coimbatore' is approximate; the Dhyanalinga stands at the Isha Yoga Center campus, Velliangiri Foothills, Semmedu (P.O.), Coimbatore 641114, about 30 km west of Coimbatore city, accessed via Poondi Main Road (coordinates are the campus anchor). Consecrated by Sadhguru Jaggi Vasudev on 24 June 1999 after a three-year prana prathista (an archived 1999 Isha notice says the consecration took place at 10:00 am IST on 25 June 1999 — date conflict flagged), and offered to the world on 23 November 1999. Claimed to be the first such consecration completed in over 2,000 years and the largest mercury-based 'live' linga in the world (13 ft 9 in), enshrining the seven chakras. A large ellipsoidal dome covers the sanctum, designed and built by architect Satprem Maini and the Auroville Earth Institute. Two subterranean Theerthakunds (solidified-mercury lingams in water) serve as preparatory meditation tanks. The Velliangiri mountains are known as the 'Kailash of the South'.
